s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive peripheral visual field blurring with corneal edema and abnormal intraocular pressures
salient_findings: Progressive peripheral visual field blurring in both eyes
Central macular scar in the left eye
Peripheral microcystic corneal edema with central corneal sparing
key_facts: Six-month history of progressive peripheral visual field blurring
Bilateral pediatric cataract surgery at age 5
Aphakia in both eyes
Central macular scar in the left eye
Family history of Fuchs’ endothelial dystrophy and microspherophakia
Uncorrected distance visual acuity was 20/250 OD and hand motion OS
Corrected distance visual acuity was 20/20 OD and hand motion OS
Intraocular pressures were 17 mmHg OD and 18.5 mmHg OS
Slit-lamp evaluation revealed peripheral microcystic corneal edema
Central corneal guttata present
Tilted optic disc OD
Grade 1 fundus tessellation OU
Central macular hyperpigmented scar OS

raw.rationale: The patient has a history of bilateral pediatric cataract surgery resulting in aphakia, and presents with peripheral microcystic corneal edema and central corneal sparing, which are characteristic findings of aphakic bullous keratopathy.

rejected.label: Fuchs' endothelial dystrophy
rejected.why: While there is a family history of Fuchs' endothelial dystrophy, the patient's presentation of peripheral microcystic corneal edema and central corneal sparing is more consistent with aphakic bullous keratopathy.

rejected.label: Pseudophakic bullous keratopathy
rejected.why: The patient is aphakic, not pseudophakic, making this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Microspherophakia
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of microspherophakia, this condition does not explain the patient's current symptoms of progressive peripheral visual field blurring and corneal edema.

rejected.label: Iridocorneal endothelial syndrome
rejected.why: There is no mention of iris or corneal abnormalities consistent with iridocorneal endothelial syndrome, making this diagnosis less likely.
